ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the FIC Act; screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficiaries and authorised agents against the domestic Specified Entities list (UN and domestic financial sanctions), OFAC SDN list where applicable per FIC guidance, and EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions for cross-border rails; enhanced due diligence mandatory for foreign politically exposed persons and their immediate family members and close associates; automatic refusal of incorporation services if a name match is confirmed, if sanctions risk cannot be mitigated, or if the beneficial owner cannot be established.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) eServices portal at https://www.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be expressed in any of the 11 official South African languages; all names must be in Latin alphabet or accurately transliterated into Latin script; Arabic and Roman numerals are permitted; the name must be capable of being represented in an ordinary Latin-character company registry; an English translation or sworn translation may be required for non-English proposed names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receiving a CIPC name rejection, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal for an administrative appeal or reconsideration under the Companies Act, 2008 and Companies Regulations, 2011. The appeal must include the CIPC reference, grounds of appeal, affidavit evidence, and the proposed corrected name, together with the prescribed filing fee. The Companies Tribunal must determine the matter within 60 days. A further appeal lies to the High Court on a question of law within 30 days of the Tribunal decision. Alternatively, the applicant may cure the defect by removing or amending the prohibited token, obtaining any required ministerial approval from the relevant competent authority, and submitting a fresh name reservation through CIPC.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is administratively acceptable for the registered office and service-of-process requirements under section 23 of the Companies Act, provided it supplies a physical street address in South Africa and is staffed for legal notice receipt. However, for ISIC 3240 manufacturing of color snap-fit plastic kits, a virtual office cannot replace the actual production premises, warehousing, and industrial inspection needed for municipal licensing, SARS registration, and customs and excise compliance; an operational physical facility in South Africa is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 20% risk of unannounced physical inspection within the first full operating year, driven primarily by the Department of Employment and Labour (factory registration and OHSA compliance), municipal fire and environmental health officers, and occasional SARS verification visits; CIPC does not routinely conduct unannounced on-site inspections of low-risk manufacturers absent a complaint.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR14.1A)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company under section 40; no escrow account rule applies
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Company adopts its Memorandum of Incorporation filed with CIPC and accepts subscriptions for 100 ordinary no-par value shares; (2) the registered office at [physical address] is approved and the Registrar is notified; (3) [Name A] and [Name B] are appointed first directors, and [Name C] is appointed managing director and public officer under the Income Tax Act; (4) the directors are empowered to open bank accounts, execute lease and supplier contracts, and complete statutory registrations for the mecha model kit manufacturing business; and (5) corporate governance operates under the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access CIPC e-Services, select Name Reservation, query name availability, if available complete CoR9.1 application, pay reservation fee and await confirmation before incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a fresh name application or file a Reconsideration Application (CoR15.4) with CIPC within 30 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Online Portal / CIPC Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name approval, complete Notice of Incorporation (CoR14.1), attach the Memorandum of Incorporation, sign via CIPC e-Services, pay filing fee, and submit; CIPC will issue a Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of ID/passport of incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any CIPC compliance query through e-Services within the prescribed 10 business days; amend the MOI and resubmit if validation errors occur.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Recording Registered Office and First Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office physical address, postal address, directors' names and identity details are correctly captured in CoR14.1; post-registration, file CoR6.1 or CoR6.2 as applicable to record any subsequent director or registered-office changes; confirm the register of members is maintained at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Change forms CoR6.1/CoR6.2 if updates are needed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC rejects a director appointment, correct the identity document and resubmit within 10 business days; in urgent cases, approach the CIPC Contact Center or use the online re-submission facility.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration and Public Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: SARS auto-registers the company for Income Tax via CIPC integration; complete the company profile update on eFiling, appoint a public officer via SARS firm profile update, register for VAT if annual taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million, and for PAYE/UIF if hiring employees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS flags verification, respond to SARS letter of demand or audit request within 21 days, provide supporting corporate documents, and use SARS Notice of Objection procedures to dispute any tax registration error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour - Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the Compensation Fund using the online e-Compass portal, obtain a letter of good standing for COIDA compliance, and register for the Unemployment Insurance Fund via SARS eFiling if employees will be engaged.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, submit manual application at provincial labour center; follow up with Compensation Fund call center; formal objection or escalation can be filed with the Compensation Board.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic) - no compulsory operating licence; optional SABS Standards Mark for voluntary product certification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating permit; voluntary SABS ISO 9001 / SANS 10118 product conformity mark

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) and competent local municipality
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration-only for standard small-scale injection moulding; full Scoping and EIA Report may be triggered only if listed waste, effluent or emission thresholds in NEMA 2014 EIA Regulations are exceeded
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with National Water Act (Act 36 of 1998) for any effluent discharge; National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act (Act 39 of 2004) for VOC emissions from paints/coatings; South African Waste Discharge Standards under Section 21 of the National Water Act; SABS SANS 10207 for hazardous waste handling if applicable

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local Fire Protection District; structural load certificate for heavy injection moulding equipment; Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993) compliance certificate; exemption from high-risk major hazard installation if chemical inventory below threshold

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); filing portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); customs via SARS Customs/SYDA (Single Administrative Document system).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the (Pty) Ltd with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) to obtain a company registration number. 2) Appoint a public officer who is a natural person resident in South Africa (mandatory under s9 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, for both resident and foreign-owned entities). 3) Register on SARS eFiling by creating a user profile and completing the RAV (Registration, Amendments and Verification) application, obtaining an Income Tax Reference Number (TIN). 4) Apply for VAT registration via the same RAV application or VAT101 form once taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory) or from ZAR 50,000 (voluntary election). 5) SARS verifies the application and issues a separate VAT registration number, SARS PIN for eFiling, and customs importer/exporter code for SYDA. 6) Foreign-owned entities must file beneficial ownership data with CIPC and maintain SARS record-keeping and public officer details; no blocked minimum capital applies to the South African (Pty) Ltd.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in South Africa; a (Pty) Ltd is a per se taxable company (resident company taxed on worldwide income at 27% headline corporate rate, lower progressive rates available only to qualifying small business corporations under s12E of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, elected/claimed in the tax return). Available elections and regimes include: (i) s12E small business corporation status for qualifying manufacturing SMEs with turnover below ZAR 20 million; (ii) s9I headquarter company election for certain qualifying 80% foreign-owned companies (not optimal for a manufacturing operating entity); (iii) voluntary VAT registration under s23(3) VAT Act 89 of 1991; (iv) functional currency election where the dominant currency is not ZAR; and (v) mandatory hybrid mismatch neutralisation rules under ss23M-23T of the Income Tax Act, which apply automatically and cannot be opted out for payments to hybrid entities or under hybrid instruments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration: ZAR 1,000,000 taxable turnover in a 12-month rolling period; voluntary VAT registration permitted from ZAR 50,000 (VAT Act 89 of 1991, s23(3)).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, smart tax devices, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing clearance. SARS eFiling is the mandatory channel for electronic submission of VAT201 returns and customs declarations (SYDA). SARS is implementing an incremental e-invoicing framework (2023-2026) aligned with the OECD-style structured e-invoice (UBL/ISO 20022) and enhanced transactional data matching, but no vendor API clearance mandate is yet in force. VAT vendors must retain full electronic records, invoices, and export proof for the prescribed period and make them available to SARS on demand; VAT returns are due monthly or bi-monthly by the 25th day following the tax period, with payment by EFT to SARS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act 89 of 1991 applies where the vendor (a VAT-registered person) supplies movable goods in the course of its enterprise and exports the goods from South Africa (or supplies them to a non-resident who exports them, with the vendor's assistance) before the expiry of 90 days after the date of issue of the tax invoice for that supply. The vendor must obtain, within 90 days after the date of export (or such extended period as the Commissioner may allow), documentary proof of export as prescribed by VAT Regulation 17, including a completed Customs Export Declaration (SAD500), transport documents (Bill of Lading or Airway Bill), commercial invoice, and, where applicable, evidence of payment in foreign currency or an inward remittance certificate. Goods must physically leave South Africa and must not be re-supplied to a resident; offshore services (e.g., design, licensing or engineering services physically performed outside South Africa) may qualify for zero-rating under s11(2)(l), subject to the vendor retaining contemporaneous proof of the foreign physical performance and customer non-residency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) lodged via SARS SYDA or an authorised customs agent
Bill of Lading (sea) or Airway Bill (air) evidencing South Africa as origin and the foreign destination
Commercial Invoice and Packing List describing the high-precision steel injection-moulded plastic model kits
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/foreign-exchange receipt (BOP/BEN form) proving payment in foreign currency
Regulation 17 supplementary proof where applicable, e.g., container/shipment tracking, terminal receipts, and customs clearance records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may deny zero-rating and issue an additional VAT assessment at 15% plus statutory interest where export documentation is missing, deficient, or inconsistent (Tax Administration Act 2011, ss187-188). Understatement penalties range from 10% to 125% of the shortfall depending on conduct (TAA ss222-223); administrative non-compliance penalties of up to ZAR 6,000 per month per non-compliance apply (TAA ss210-213). Retrospective reassessment periods are generally 3 years in 'clean' cases, 5 years for negligence/substantial understatement, and unlimited where fraud, misrepresentation, or deliberate evasion is established (TAA s99). Fraudulent or reckless export zero-rating claims attract criminal liability under VAT Act s58 and TAA s234, with fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years, plus customs penalties under the Customs Control Act 31 of 2014 for false export declarations. SARS may also claw back refunds with interest and, where a pattern of unjustified refund claims exists, impose a 'repeating' penalty of up to 200% of the assessed tax on certain transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as the central bank and exchange control authority in terms of the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 and the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a partially liberalised exchange control system. Current account transactions, including trade-related payments, are freely convertible via authorised dealers. Capital account transactions are subject to case-by-case approval and reporting, with the rand as the domestic settlement currency. Dividend remittances to non-residents are permitted under a Dividend Remittance Procedure requiring proof of investment, the company's tax registration qualifications, a listing of actual shareholding, and Payment of Dividends Tax before outward transfer. The principal remittance hurdles are SARS tax clearance compliance, debt obligation reporting, and the completion of the BOP form for stationary versus trade-related remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must on-board a valid Foreign Currency Export Contract (FCEC) with the authorised dealer before final shipment. The full invoice value of exported goods must be received within 180 days from the date of shipment, or within such extended period as the authorised dealer may approve. All export proceeds received in foreign currency must be surrendered to the authorised dealer for conversion into rand, unless the dealer approves a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) on demonstration of cash-flow needs. A 100% conversion is the statutory default for the portion not retained in a FCA.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First National Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. South African banking law under the Banks Act, 94 of 1990 requires deposit-taking or payment clearing linkage to a licensed bank as a regulated financial institution. Offshore digital EMI or payment service providers may on-board South African-based entities only to the extent they have entered into formal agency or collaboration agreements with a licensed South African bank. For a cash-flow stabilised manufacturing entity, EMIs are viable for payment collection APIs and payouts into a domestic bank account, but cannot replace a Tier-1 local banking relationship for foreign currency conversion and settlement. PayPal is accepted as a low-value trade disbursement gateway, and is classified as a payment method with no bank-grade settlement function.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA), directors and beneficial owners of corporate clients must undergo a risk-sensitive verification. Most Tier-1 banks accept remote or digital onboarding for low-risk manufacturing entities, provided a virtual identity verification (biometric and liveness) and a video-recorded interview are conducted for the mandated director or authorised signatory. High-risk jurisdictions, non-resident ownership above 50%, or unusual source-of-funds patterns trigger a face-to-face interview at the bank's office. A locally placed director or a notarised attestation from a registered foreign bank also satisfies the physical attestation requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder is a non-resident individual or corporate; source of the initial capital injection is not clearly documented.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company and Shareholding Register with trust deed, deed of incorporation or resolution of foreign corporate, passport, a notarised bank reference letter from the remitting bank, and a sworn statement of source of wealth (family wealth, dividend, salary, or liquidation).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Contradiction between the registered trading address and the physical manufacturing plant; SARS eFiling address mismatch or transshipment indicator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SARS Income Tax Clearance Certificate, proof of business premise (municipal rate, rental invoice, utility bill), approved structural building plans or factory gate photo, and a notarised ‘physical presence’ signature from the accounting officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Onboarding request for a standard operational account is accompanied by export proceeds to non-aligned third-party debtors, and the bank cannot assess business rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Schedules of clients/principal purchase orders, underlying sales invoices and customs declarations (Bill of Entry), a copy of the FCEC, and a treasury-proof description of the product (plastic model kits with HS/ISIC reference), plus a tax clearance PIN from SARS.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injection by non-resident investor(s) is classified as a capital transaction requiring inward verification. The routing is a SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident remitter to a Tier-1 bank account, referencing 'Foreign Direct Investment in Proprietary Limited – ISIC_3240' and supplying the correct BOP purpose code (equity participation). The payment instruction must include the Investor’s registered name, the operational entity, the purpose of investment, and a written exchange-control declaration that the remittance is not underwritten from South African sourced funds. The authorised dealer verifies the source of funds, completes a Foreign Exchange Declaration, and reports to FinSurv for post-transaction validation. A preferential route is to use the company's statutory capital escrow account, which is opened exclusively for inward equity, and then to transfer to the operating account after compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 executed through the authorised dealer for raw material imports and royalty payments. For commercial letters of credit, SWIFT MT700 series are used for open-account-backed documentary credit, with payment released upon presentation of title documents. Domestic clearing for lower-value cross-border invoices is processed through the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) system and SADC regional payment systems; PayPal commercial transactions resemble ‘open invoice rail’ but are not considered a bank clearing rail. All outbound settlements must reference the underlying transaction, evidence the service or goods, and satisfy the largest exporter reporting descriptions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency option (premium priced or zero-cost collar)
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) where an underlying commercial or financial exposure requires settlement in a different currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, s33) - consolidated confirmation of registered office, directors, shareholders, auditor (if any), and beneficial ownership declaration, together with turnover band declaration for fee assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Pretoria, South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation (s33(3)); recurring annually on same anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accruing penalty fees of ZAR 225 (1 year overdue), ZAR 450 (2 years), ZAR 675 (3 years), ZAR 900 (4 years), and ZAR 1,125 (5+ years); failure to file for two consecutive years marks the company 'in default' and triggers CIPC administrative strike-off/deregistration under s82(3) after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) - prepared, approved by the board, and passed to shareholders per s30 and s31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the company (CIPC filing not required unless specifically directed by regulation or a CIPC compliance notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year (s30(4)); delivered to every shareholder within 15 business days after board approval (s30(4A))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under s30 read with s216: the company is liable to a fine up to ZAR 20,000 per contravention; directors who knowingly fail may be liable to a fine up to ZAR 1,000,000 or imprisonment, with continued default leading to CIPC compliance notice and default status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Interest (BOI) declaration - annual confirmation of every natural person holding a beneficial interest in the company (s56, amended by General Laws (AML/CFT) Amendment Act 22 of 2022)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register (electronic filing via e-CIPC portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual return within 30 business days of the incorporation anniversary; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 7 days of the change (s56(3))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The annual return will not be accepted while the BOI schedule is outstanding; knowing non-compliance is a criminal offence carrying a fine or imprisonment up to 10 years (General Laws Amendment Act 2022); directors and the company face administrative fines up to ZAR 20,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Public Interest Score (PIS) calculation and audit/review exemption determination (s30(2A) and Regulation 29)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors (recorded in board minutes; no standalone statutory filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Recomputed at each financial year end; the score sheet and supporting AFS records must be retained for the statutory 7-year period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misstatement or understatement of the PIS to evade audit or independent review invalidates reliance on the exemption; CIPC may retroactively compel audited AFS and the directors are exposed to personal liability for loss suffered by the company or shareholders

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more (s30(2A)(a)); independent review required if PIS is 100 to 349 unless shareholders elect a full audit (s30(2A)(b)); no audit or review required below PIS 100 unless the company is a state-owned company, holds assets in a fiduciary capacity in excess of ZAR 5 million, is owned by a public entity, or is otherwise declared to be in the public interest; any shareholder may nonetheless require an audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for listed companies and public interest entities; IFRS for SMEs for most private (Pty) Ltd companies; annual financial statements must present the company's financial position fairly per s29 and be approved and dated by the board under s30

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return requires the company to confirm that its Beneficial Ownership Register is complete, accurate, and current; every share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the company's Beneficial Ownership Register and the BOI declaration must be amended and filed with CIPC within 7 days of the change; the annual return submission on the incorporation anniversary serves as the annual confirmation snapshot, and beneficial ownership records must be retained for 7 years after the cessation of ownership

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 170 - 830 (ZAR 3,000 - 15,000) per annum for outsourced registered office, company secretarial administration, and annual return preparation/filing services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 3,000 for an independent review; USD 3,500 - 8,000 for a full statutory audit at a mid-tier South African firm for a small-to-medium manufacturing entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; reduced from 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: s.12C accelerated depreciation (40% first-year allowance on new manufacturing plant/machinery; 20% per annum on used assets); s.11D R&D super-deduction (150% of qualifying expenditure); s.12I (Industrial Policy Projects) allowance; Small Business Corporation graduated rates (0%/7%/21%/27%) for turnover ≤ ZAR 20 million; s.12H learnership allowance
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward; set-off capped at 80% of taxable income for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 January 2024 (Taxation Laws Amendment Act 2023)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Income Tax Return for Companies) via SARS eFiling portal (with Auto-Assessments for certain low-risk filings)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (IRP6 provisional estimates: first payment due 6 months after start of year of assessment; second payment due on last business day of 6th month after year-end; optional third top-up payment)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return due within 12 months after the financial year-end (SARS may issue a Notice demanding earlier filing; the deadline is generally the last day of the month falling 12 months after year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS tax reference number, registered name, trading name, registration number, postal/registered address, financial year-end, status of company (resident/non-resident)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the company's place of effective management (POEM); if a foreign-owned SA branch, annex an IRP6/ITR14 branch return and submit the audited financial statements of the foreign head office

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from sale of action-figure model kits, mecha kits and related accessories, excluding VAT; include export sales, PayPal/SWIFT receipts, and any gross rents/royalties received
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report turnover gross of any cross-border related-party commissions; attach a reconciliation of amounts settled through offshore payment rails

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SA-source dividends (s.10(1)(k)), certain interest exemptions (s.10(1)(i)), and other exempt receipts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' distributions are not deductible to the company; dividends are subject to 20% dividend tax unless a DTA declaration was lodged

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, resin/steel raw materials, mould tooling depreciation, factory wages, packaging, freight, insurance, and allocable overheads; s.11(a) general deduction for expenses incurred in the production of income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallowable: payments to foreign related parties that fail the s.31 transfer-pricing arm's length test; withholding taxes (royalty/interest) are not deductible; s.23I limits interest deductions where debt-to-equity ratios and EBIT-safe-harbours are exceeded

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of assessed loss brought forward from prior year less taxable income of current year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: From 1 January 2024, only 80% of taxable income may be offset by an assessed loss; remaining balance carries forward indefinitely

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and normal tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income x 27% = normal tax; deduct s.6quat foreign tax credits, s.6bis rebates, and provisional tax payments (IRP6) already made; balance payable or refundable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the 'rebates and credits' schedule with detailed schedules for foreign tax credits; SARS requires proof of foreign tax paid (assessment notice, TRC or tax receipt)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative non-compliance penalty under TAA s.210 of ZAR 250 per day (capped at ZAR 4,500 per month) for the highest band; SARS may raise an estimated assessment (TAA s.95) with an additional 10% penalty on the estimated tax; understatement penalties of 10%–150% of the shortfall (TAA s.222–223); interest at the prescribed rate (repo + 4%) runs from the effective date of the assessment; provisional underestimation penalty of 20% of the tax on the shortfall where an estimate is below 80% (first estimate) or 90% (second estimate) of actual taxable income

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (in effect for dividends paid on or after 22 February 2017; former rate 15%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must complete SARS Form DTD (declaration) and submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) to the company/withholding agent before the dividend payment date; the reduced treaty rate is applied at source. If 20% was withheld in error, the shareholder must file a refund claim with SARS within three years, furnishing the DTD, TRC, dividend statement and proof of residence; the company remains liable to pay the 20% dividend tax over to SARS if it fails to withhold (with 10% penalty and interest).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: royalties 15% (s.49B Income Tax Act), interest 15% (s.50B). Treaty: frequently reduced to 0%–10% (e.g., SA–US DTA provides 0% on most royalties and interest; SA–UK DTA provides 0% on royalties and interest for beneficial owners). Reduced rates require the same DTD + TRC protocol before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File/Master File: no statutory de minimis; SARS requires contemporaneous arm's length documentation for all cross-border related-party transactions, and practical guidance expects documentation where individual/aggregate transactions exceed ZAR 5 million per year. CbCR: mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue of at least ZAR 10 billion (≈ EUR 750 million); notification and Master File/Local File via SARS eFiling with year-end filings.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No Gulf/Caribbean-style ESR statute is enacted. Substance is enforced through: (i) the OECD BEPS Principal Purpose Test (PPT) incorporated via the MLI in double-tax agreements; (ii) the s.9D CFC regime (attribution of tainted income to SA shareholders); (iii) GAAR under s.80A–80L; and (iv) the central-management-and-control test for corporate residence (s.1 Income Tax Act). A local manufacturer must maintain real premises, active board decisions, operational payroll, and local production/tooling substance to access treaty benefits and avoid being re-characterised as a shell or conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating turnover from PayPal/SWIFT sales of mecha model kits, inflating mould-tooling costs, manufacturing fictitious deductions, or destroying sales records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty of 150% of the shortfall for intentional evasion (TAA s.223); criminal conviction on indictment: fine (court's discretion) and/or imprisonment up to 5 years (TAA s.235); interest at repo + 4%
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly cause or permit the evasion are jointly liable under the common-law piercing doctrine and s.77(3) Companies Act; personal civil restitution, a SARS travel ban under TAA s.194–196 (no departure without tax clearance or security), asset attachment, and imprisonment up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Offshore Shell Intermediary
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive 'character licence' royalties or management fees to a zero-tax related IP-holding company in a black-listed jurisdiction with no employees, premises, or active decision-making; routing export sales through a low-trade-tax related distributor at a loss-making margin
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS adjustment to arm's length consideration under s.31; understatement penalty of 50% (no reasonable grounds) to 150% (intentional evasion); interest; CFC inclusion under s.9D if the offshore entity is a CFC; denial of treaty benefits under the PPT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's-length arrangements face personal liability for reckless trading (Companies Act s.22 read with s.77); SARS can pierce the veil and recover the adjusted tax, plus travel bans and potential disqualification as directors

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder without withholding 20% dividend tax, or applying a treaty rate without obtaining the DTD declaration and TRC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company as withholding agent remains liable for the full 20% tax (s.46A/57 Income Tax Act), plus a 10% penalty and prescribed interest; failure to register/maintain accurate dividend records attracts ANP penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: SARS may recover the unwithheld tax from directors who were responsible for the payment and knowingly failed to withhold; personal liability via TAA s.154 (representative taxpayer provisions), interest, and criminal exposure under TAA s.234 for repeated non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Companies Act s.56 beneficial-interest register, permitting third-party deposits into company bank accounts without source-of-funds scrutiny, or facilitating laundering through PayPal/SWIFT rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial Intelligence Centre administrative sanction of up to ZAR 50 million per contravention (or a turnover-based amount); criminal conviction: unlimited fine and/or imprisonment up to 15 years (FICA s.68); deregistration or responsible-clerk orders under the Companies Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for knowingly allowing the company to be used for money laundering; civil asset forfeiture under POCA, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 15 years; disqualification as company directors under s.69 Companies Act

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Trading while technically insolvent, applying PAYE/provisional tax collections to fund working capital, or paying out dividends while liabilities (including SARS debt) exceed assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prohibition under s.22(1) Companies Act; SARS may wind up the company; interest and penalties for unpaid provisional tax/PAYE; statutory preference for SARS in insolvency (preferential claim for employees' tax)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability for all debts (including tax) if the company is traded recklessly, with gross negligence, or fraudulently (s.77(3)(b) read with s.22); civil claims by SARS as a creditor, sequestration/bankruptcy of directors, travel bans, and imprisonment for up to 10 years for fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Classifying injection-moulding and assembly-line workers as independent contractors or foreign freelancers to avoid PAYE, UIF, SDL and COIDA obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS re-characterisation under the 'dominant impression' test; recovery of un-withheld PAYE (TAA s.156–160), s.210 ANP penalties, 200% deemed-employer penalty in aggravated cases, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors qualify as 'representative taxpayers' and can be held personally liable for all unremitted employees' tax (TAA s.159); criminal liability for failure to withhold or pay over; travel bans and director disqualification apply
